subject.title: Feature: Postcondition checks for cron jobs (deterministic verification of agent outcomes)

question: Should cron post-run verification be a scheduler-owned bounded verifier contract, a plugin-owned fail-capable hook, or deferred to a broader agent outcome-verification design?
rationale: The source proves the capability is missing, but adding it directly changes core cron semantics and introduces command-execution/security and retry-policy choices that automation should not decide.

options.title: Add bounded scheduler verifier
options.body: Define an additive cron postcondition contract in core with typed state, strict execution limits, retry/escalation behavior, and security review before implementation.

options.title: Add fail-capable plugin hook
options.body: Keep core lean by first adding a supported post-run hook that can fail a cron run and request scheduler-owned retry or escalation.

options.title: Defer to broader verification design
options.body: Leave this issue open but pause implementation until maintainers settle a shared verification model across cron, channel delivery, and agent finalization.

recommendation.title: Add bounded scheduler verifier
recommendation.body: Define an additive cron postcondition contract in core with typed state, strict execution limits, retry/escalation behavior, and security review before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They already reviewed this issue and are the strongest identified maintainer-side owner for the cron product decision.
